hints: Focus on whether each Period 3 oxide actually dissolves and reacts with water, because no reaction means no change in pH.
Recall that $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ is insoluble and $\text{SiO}_2$ is a giant covalent solid that does not react with water.
Contrast those two with $\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$, which reacts vigorously to form a strong acid solution, then pick the combination with only the non-reacting oxides.
walkthrough:
**Ask what changes pH**

A solid only changes the pH of water if it dissolves and then releases $\text{H}^+$ or $\text{OH}^-$ ions. If it is insoluble and does not react, the pH stays at 7.

Rule to use:
$$\text{acidic oxide + water} \rightarrow \text{acidic solution, pH < 7}$$

**Check aluminium oxide and silicon dioxide**

$\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ is amphoteric but essentially insoluble in water, so it just sits as a solid. $\text{SiO}_2$ is acidic in character but has a giant covalent lattice that water cannot break, so it also does not react.

Conclusion:
$$\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3(s) + \text{H}_2\text{O}(l) \rightarrow \text{no reaction}$$
$$\text{SiO}_2(s) + \text{H}_2\text{O}(l) \rightarrow \text{no reaction}$$

**Check phosphorus(V) oxide**

$\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$ is a covalent molecular oxide that reacts fully with water to give phosphoric acid, a weak acid that releases $\text{H}^+$.

Equation:
$$\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}(s) + 6\text{H}_2\text{O}(l) \rightarrow 4\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4(aq)$$

**Combine the conclusion**

Oxides 1 and 2 cause no reaction and no pH change, while oxide 3 causes an acidic solution with pH well below 7. So the correct combination is 1 and 2 only.

options.A: Incorrect because it includes all three oxides. $\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$ does react to form $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$ and lowers the pH, so it cannot be in the 'no change' list.
options.B: Correct because both $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ and $\text{SiO}_2$ are insoluble and do not react with water, so pH remains at 7. Only $\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$ is excluded as it forms an acidic solution.
options.C: Incorrect because it pairs $\text{SiO}_2$ with $\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$. $\text{SiO}_2$ is correct to include, but $\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$ strongly acidifies water, so this combination is wrong.
options.D: Incorrect because it lists only 1. $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ alone is indeed no change, but $\text{SiO}_2$ also causes no change and has been missed. Students choosing this often think all acidic oxides react with water.
